title: Data Use and Sharing
text: You must receive explicit permission from users via the App Tracking Transparency APIs to track their activity. You must clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties (including third-party AI) and obtain explicit permission before doing so. Data collected from apps may only be shared with third parties to improve the app or serve advertising in compliance with the Apple Developer Program License Agreement.

title: Data Collection and Storage
text: Apps must request access to personal data (such as location, contacts, calendars, photos, camera, microphone, Bluetooth) only when relevant to core functionality, and must provide a clear, specific purpose string explaining how the data is used. Apps must include a link to their privacy policy and clearly identify what data is collected, how, and all uses. Empty or generic purpose strings are not acceptable.

title: Account Sign-In and Deletion
text: Apps that support account creation must also offer account deletion initiated from within the app, allowing users to delete their account and associated personal data, not merely deactivate it or contact support.

title: In-App Purchase
text: To unlock features or functionality within an app (subscriptions, in-game currencies, premium content, unlocking a full version), you must use in-app purchase. Apps may not use their own mechanisms (license keys, QR codes, cryptocurrencies) to unlock content. Except on the United States storefront or via approved StoreKit External Purchase Link entitlements, apps and their metadata may not include buttons, external links, or calls to action directing customers to purchasing mechanisms other than in-app purchase.

title: Health and Health Research
text: Apps may not use or disclose to third parties data gathered in the health, fitness, and medical research context (including HealthKit) for advertising, marketing, or use-based data mining other than improving health management or health research, and then only with permission. Apps must not write false or inaccurate data into HealthKit and may not store personal health information in iCloud. You must disclose the specific health data you collect.

title: Background Execution
text: Multitasking apps may only use background services for their intended purposes (e.g. VoIP, audio playback, location, task completion, local notifications). Declaring background modes such as location, audio, or voip that the app does not genuinely require for an active, user-facing feature is grounds for rejection.

title: Self-Contained Software and Security
text: Apps should be self-contained and may not download, install, or execute code that changes features or functionality. Secrets, private keys, and credentials must not be embedded in the app binary or source, since material distributed in the binary can be extracted; store secrets securely and rotate any that are exposed.

title: Minimum Functionality
text: Your app should include features, content, and UI that elevate it beyond a repackaged website. If your app is not particularly useful, unique, or app-like, or simply mirrors a website with little native functionality, it does not belong on the App Store.

title: Login Services
text: Apps that use a third-party or social login service (e.g. Facebook, Google) to set up or authenticate the user's primary account must also offer an equivalent login option that limits data collection to name and email, lets users keep their email private, and does not collect interactions for advertising without consent (e.g. Sign in with Apple). Exceptions apply for apps using only their own account system, education/enterprise apps, and certain others.

title: User-Generated Content
text: Apps with user-generated content or social networking must include: a method for filtering objectionable material from being posted, a mechanism to report offensive content with timely responses, the ability to block abusive users, and published contact information.

title: Privacy Manifest Files
text: Apps and third-party SDKs that use required-reason APIs (e.g. UserDefaults, file timestamps, system boot time, disk space) or collect data must include a privacy manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) declaring the collected data types and the approved reasons for using those APIs. Missing or incomplete manifests for tracking SDKs can block submission.

title: App Privacy Details on the App Store
text: App Store privacy labels (App Privacy details in App Store Connect) must accurately reflect the data the app and its third-party SDKs collect and how it is used. New data collection or sharing must be reflected in these labels.

title: Preventing Insecure Network Connections
text: App Transport Security (ATS) requires network connections to use secure HTTPS/TLS. Disabling ATS globally via NSAllowsArbitraryLoads, or adding broad cleartext HTTP exceptions without documented justification, weakens user security and can lead to rejection. Scope any exceptions as narrowly as possible.

title: Payments policy
text: Developers offering in-app purchases of digital goods or content consumed within an app obtained from Google Play must use Google Play's billing system, unless an exception applies. Directing users to alternative payment methods for in-app digital purchases, or using a non-Play billing system without eligibility, is not permitted.

title: Data deletion
text: Apps that allow account creation must provide users a way to request deletion of their account and associated data both from within the app and via a web resource, and must surface these data-deletion options in the store listing's Data safety section.

title: Permissions and APIs that Access Sensitive Information
text: Requests for permissions and APIs that access sensitive information must be limited to what is necessary for current, disclosed features. High-risk or sensitive permissions (e.g. background location, SMS or Call Log, All files access / MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, package visibility / QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES) are subject to additional declarations and approved-use-case requirements.

title: Foreground services policy
text: Apps targeting Android 14 (API 34) and above must declare an appropriate foregroundServiceType for each foreground service and request the matching FOREGROUND_SERVICE_* permission. The declared type must correspond to an approved use case; foreground services used outside the permitted types are not allowed.

title: Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section
text: Developers must complete the Data safety form accurately, declaring what user data the app collects and shares and for what purposes, reflecting actual behavior including third-party SDKs. Introducing new data collection or sharing without updating the Data safety section is a policy violation.

title: Spam and minimum functionality
text: Apps that provide little or no functionality, are primarily a webview or wrapper of a website, or repackage web content with minimal native value may be rejected for failing minimum functionality and webview/web-app requirements.

title: User data
text: Apps must handle personal and sensitive user data securely, including transmission over modern cryptography (HTTPS). Enabling cleartext (unencrypted HTTP) traffic via android:usesCleartextTraffic or broad network-security-config exceptions without justification exposes user data and may violate Play's User Data and security policies.

title: User-generated content policy
text: Apps featuring user-generated content must implement effective UGC moderation: a way to report content and block users, content filtering, and timely removal of objectionable content. Apps that fail to address objectionable UGC may be removed from Google Play.

title: Meet Google Play's target API level requirement
text: When you upload an APK or app bundle, it must meet Google Play's target API level requirements. Starting August 31, 2026, new apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher to be submitted to Google Play, except Wear OS and Android Automotive OS apps (Android 15 / API 35+) and Android TV and Android XR apps (Android 14 / API 34+). Existing apps must target Android 15 (API level 35) or higher to remain available to new users on devices running a newer Android OS than the app's target API level. Apps that target lower API levels will only be available on devices running Android OS at or below the app's target level.
